title: Profiling memory and time on a GPU (with a CPU model of it)
hook: A peak isn't the sum of your tensors, and the slowest thing isn't always where you look. Learn to read both before you change anything.

verified.claim: nvidia-smi can show memory held by PyTorch's caching allocator as used; memory_allocated tracks tensors and memory_reserved what the allocator holds; empty_cache releases unused cached memory.
GPU operations are asynchronous by default, so timings need care.
GET /system_stats returns vram_total, vram_free, torch_vram_total and torch_vram_free per device.
On an out-of-memory error ComfyUI logs torch.cuda.memory.memory_summary on NVIDIA and AMD.
ComfyUI prints Prompt executed in N seconds for each job, and keeps a timestamp per log write.
Peaks and bytes in the Lab come from a run here. Sizes and times are examples we chose.

unchecked: We ran no GPU profile for this lesson, and no number here describes a real model's peak.
We did not read how Dynamic VRAM's memory is reported to torch or nvidia-smi, so a reading on that path may differ from what the allocator model suggests.
The toy allocator keeps the idea of reserved memory and leaves out everything else a real allocator does.
